lead: the phone goes at seven and you are standing in their kitchen by nine, and the job that starts that fast runs a season past the date you gave them, every time, for reasons nobody on site can see.
sun: you are on the tools and you are the one who prices the work. both are the trade at full standard, and neither is the one you kept your hand in at while doing the other. the week divides itself between the ladder and the phone, and a fortnight of dropping either end shows up in the other end within the month, so it has never been dropped.
moon: the speed sits entirely at the front. you are through their door before the other two firms have returned a call, and the price is with them that night. arriving quickly is the one thing here the doubleness has never slowed, and it goes at that pace every time, so every customer you have had met the fast one first and priced their patience off it.
pull: every customer meets you at your fastest and pays you at your slowest. the arrival takes one person, the work takes two, and you are both of them.
tension: slow comes back to you from people who like you. a customer whose price you wrote in one night waits three weeks for a decision that needs you off the ladder. the advice is always the same and always kindly meant: put somebody else on the phone, stick to the tools. what that would do is take the firm apart. the price gets trusted because the person quoting it is the person who will be fitting it.
cost: a price set by the hand that will do the work, and a first visit inside two hours: the trade does not hand a customer both, and you have never given one without the other. the firm has run three years behind since you were thirty-four, and the two who trained with you each took an end and each runs four jobs to your one.

lead: everything in your life arrived with its opposite number attached and got carried both ways at once. one thing did not. it has been in you a long time and it has never had a second half.
sun: count fourteen stations off your sun in one direction and you land on your moon; count fourteen the other way and you land on it again. the fork even goes two ways about where the far end of you is, and there is nowhere further to put it on this wheel. so the two-way carry runs the whole of your outward life and stops dead at the one place that holds.
moon: what holds in you holds one thing, and it stands where the doubling cannot reach. it has never learned the two-way carry, so the item you keep is the only unforked thing you own. every competence you have is for running two at once, and none of it applies here. the release date sits with a part of you that has never had to carry anything twice.
pull: you can carry any two things for as long as they need. the one thing you have kept alone sits at the far end of the road from everything you know how to do.
tension: people who know you describe an open person with one closed room. ask about anything you are carrying two ways and you will go for an hour, evenly. ask about this and there is nothing, and the drop is steep enough to read as concealment. what sits there has never had a second side to set against it, so any account of it would come out single, and single is the one thing you have never said out loud.
cost: two of anything can run in you for decades without either one thinning, which is why nobody around you has ever had to be the only one. the single thing gets none of that. it is unpaired, and there is no second version to release in its place, so it waits on a decision you have never had to make, and nothing in you is practised at making it.

lead: there is one figure for what you make and it has never been true. two things you own are funded out of the same account, each has spent years paying for the other, and neither has been the hobby.
sun: both of them get real money and real years. the boat paid the practice's rent through two bad winters, and the practice covered an engine and a full refit the year the bookings did not come. that is one arrangement rather than a business with a sideline attached, and taking either out does not leave a smaller version of the same living. it leaves the other one without capital inside a season.
moon: from any distance there is one self-employed person doing all right. the bank sees a single applicant and the family sees a single livelihood, and both readings come off numbers that exist only because two separate concerns get added together on one return. look properly and it resolves into two undercapitalised businesses, each rescued more than once by the other, neither of which would stand a look alone.
pull: one figure goes on every form and no single business has ever stood behind it. each half has bailed the other out, and each on its own looks like something to close.
tension: the question comes once a year, from an accountant or a brother-in-law, and it always arrives as arithmetic: which of these actually makes money, and why are you carrying the other. no answer you have fits that shape. the true one needs both sets of books open together and eleven years of dates showing which way the rescues ran, and before you have the second folder out the person asking has settled it privately, and settled it as sentiment.
cost: nothing you own has ever folded, and the reason is that no single downturn has hit both at the same time — a rescue was always available from the side that was working. what neither has ever had is a year of its own full capital. both are the size they were at thirty, and whatever either could have grown into went into keeping the other one standing.

lead: half the year you eat to get bigger and half the year you eat to get smaller, and both are hunger rather than discipline. the shape you are aiming at belongs to a man you last saw at twenty-three.
sun: the two directions are equally real in the body and equally wanted. in the building months you want the food and actually want it; in the stripping months you want the lightness with the same appetite, and neither craving is the discipline keeping the other down. the year has two hungers in it and no neutral month anywhere, and both are the training. neither end arrives early.
moon: the standard never moves and it never got two versions. one body, seen at twenty-three, and everything since has been measured against that single mark from a fixed distance behind it. so the fork runs in the method and stops at the target: two seasons, two appetites, one shape, and the shape was set by somebody who has no idea he set it and would not recognise you now.
pull: two directions of hunger a year apart, and both of them are real. the body you are working towards has been the same one since you were twenty-three.
tension: nobody sees a person who is always mid-something, which is what you are; they see a weight that goes up and down and they have a word for that. your sister has used it twice. the doctor uses a chart. the version where both directions are deliberate and both are being trained sounds, out loud, exactly like what somebody would say who could not hold a line, and the graph on the screen supports them rather than you.
cost: at forty-one you can still train hard in either direction, in any month of the year, and the body does both without complaint. the finished thing has never been seen. every photograph of you is halfway up or halfway down, and thirty years of work is aimed at a body that has never once existed on any given day.
